data.description:
## Summary

`run_http_with_grace` sets uvicorn's `timeout_graceful_shutdown` to the SAME value as the
certified-op drain grace (`_mcp_health.py:217`, `timeout_graceful_shutdown=int(grace_seconds)`,
`DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS = 1200`). Its own docstring calls that timeout "a backstop" —
but for a Streamable-HTTP MCP server it is the OPERATIVE timer on every retirement, because a
connected MCP client holds a long-lived stream that never closes on its own. uvicorn's graceful
shutdown waits for that stream until the timeout expires.

The result: a retiring mcp container ALWAYS takes the full 1200s to exit whenever any client
holds a session — which, for a dogfooding server that agents connect to, is the normal steady
state. The gauge-driven early exit that the design is built around never fires.

## Why this defeats the documented design

The intended model is explicit in the code:

- `drain_then_exit` (`_mcp_health.py:134-150`): "Wait (bounded by `grace_seconds`) for the gauge
  to reach 0 ... **Returns immediately when the gauge is already idle.**"
- `make_sigterm_handler` (`:153-178`): stop intake first, "keeps a newly-arriving op from
  extending the drain window indefinitely".
- `run_http_with_grace` (`:195`): "`timeout_graceful_shutdown` bounds uvicorn's own drain **as a
  backstop**."

So the gauge is meant to be the primary bound and uvicorn's timeout the safety net. In practice
the safety net governs 100% of the time and the entire gauge apparatus (`InFlightGauge`,
`instrument_certified_tools`, the `/health` `in_flight` field, `drain_then_exit`'s early return)
has no effect on when the process exits.

## Runtime proof (discriminating experiment)

A minimal uvicorn app with `timeout_graceful_shutdown=5`, an endless streaming route, and
**gauge == 0 in both arms** (no certified op anywhere):

```
NO open stream   -> exited in   0.18s
ONE open stream  -> exited in   5.39s     <- the full timeout
uvicorn: "Cancel 1 running task(s), timeout graceful shutdown exceeded"
```

This discriminates against the rival hypothesis (a leaked in-flight gauge): the gauge was zero
and the wait happened anyway. It is the open connection, not the gauge, that pins the shutdown.

## Production evidence, matching the prediction to the second

Container `rebar-mcp-1efc5ebb57dd-8092` on `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (2026-08-26):

| event | time |
|---|---|
| first `docker stop --time 1260` issued | 18:25:08 |
| container `die` | 18:45:09 |
| reaped by the next tick | 18:46:24 |

18:45:09 - 18:25:08 = **1200s exactly** = `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`, not the 1260s docker
deadline. The process burned its own full grace and exited a second after it expired.

Corroborating: `docker events` shows SIGTERM (`signal=15`) delivered **7 times**, once per
~2-minute autodeploy tick (deltas 130/129/121/120/121/129s) — each tick re-issues the stop via
`mcp_retire_graceful` with no already-stopping guard. These are harmless (each merely re-sets
`should_exit`) and notably did NOT reset the drain deadline, which is what pins the cause to the
first SIGTERM's uvicorn timeout rather than to handler re-entry.

## Impact: a hard ceiling of ~one mcp deploy per 20 minutes

The blue/green pool is exactly two host ports (`autodeploy.sh:129`, 8092/8093; 8091 reserved).
The live container permanently holds one. A retiring container now holds the other for a full
20 minutes. So a second mcp deploy inside that window finds no free port:

`autodeploy.sh:670-674` — `mcp_free_port` returns empty, and the deploy emits
`AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP port-exhausted`, records backoff, and exits 1.

It fails SAFE (no port collision, live backend untouched), so this is a throughput defect, not a
correctness or availability one. But it caps mcp deploys at roughly one per 20 minutes, and it
does so for a wait that the design intended to be near-instant when no certified op is running.

## Not the reported symptom

Filed after investigating "container Up 2 hours (unhealthy)". That framing was wrong and is NOT
a defect: `docker ps` "Up" reports total uptime since creation, and that container was the LIVE
backend for ~1h45m before the 18:25 cutover. The "unhealthy" flag is also expected — SIGTERM
stops intake, so the healthcheck is refused for the rest of the drain. Only the 1200s-always
drain underneath is a real defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A retiring mcp process with `gauge == 0` exits promptly (seconds, not the full grace) even
      while a client holds an open streamable-HTTP session.
- [ ] An in-flight CERTIFIED op still delays exit up to the grace bound — the drain guarantee
      that `mcp_retire_graceful` and ADR 0079 depend on is preserved, not traded away.
- [ ] A regression test pins the distinction (open-but-idle stream => prompt exit; in-flight
      certified op => waits), failing if `timeout_graceful_shutdown` is re-coupled to
      `grace_seconds`.
- [ ] Deploying mcp twice inside one drain window no longer emits `port-exhausted`.
data.title: mcp retirement always burns the full 1200s drain: uvicorn timeout_graceful_shutdown is coupled to the certified-op grace
